on_tick.turn: align_gain * IF(NEAR("$Boids", radius) > 0, ((NEAR_HEADING("$Boids", radius) - self.heading + 540) % 360 - 180), 0) + NORM(0, noise_sd)

info.description: Reynolds/Vicsek-style flocking: 150 Boid agents in a 100x100 wrapped continuous space, each turning each tick toward NEAR_HEADING (the circular mean heading of neighbours within Radius) plus a little noise, then stepping Speed forward -- alignment only, so the effect measured is alignment alone. Each boid keeps its unit heading vector (ux, uy) = (COS(RAD(heading)), SIN(RAD(heading))) and `polar`, the textbook POLARISATION order parameter: the norm of the flock's mean unit heading, SQRT(MEAN(ux)^2 + MEAN(uy)^2) -- about 1/SQRT(N) (0.07 for 150) for random headings, 1 for a perfectly aligned flock. A synchronous tick reads the tick-start snapshot, so `polar` after tick k measures the headings of tick k - 1. With Align gain 0.3 and Noise sd 6 degrees it climbs from the random baseline past 0.9 within 60 ticks. Radius, Align gain, Noise sd and Speed are this instance's own.
